messages:
morgan: Heads-up - noticed a spike in the quota dashboard for "projectless" API keys this morning. Looks like a bunch of requests are being attributed to the org default project and it's blowing the per-project quota. Anyone seen this behavior before?
lee: Saw similar on staging last week. Routing logic defaults to org fallback when project claim missing. Intended but probably not what teams expect. :grimacing:
anya: Can you paste an example request header and the dashboard row?
morgan: snippet: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_projless_abc123" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'```
jordyn: Ops-bot alerted around 03:10 UTC: "Quota alert: project default-42 is at 92%" for many tenants. Seems correlated to onboarding scripts that use org-scoped keys.
samir: Quick summary of current routing precedence: 1) explicit project claim in key 2) project header X-Redwood-Project 3) origin-project header 4) fallback to org-default project. That's in code, but one-off keys often skip the claim so fallthrough happens.
morgan: The concern is twofold: (1) noisy quota headaches for existing projects, (2) billing/ownership confusion for customers. We should avoid attributing to prod projects silently.
lee: Options: A) stop attributing to a project unless claim exists (traffic becomes projectless but shows in org-line items) B) keep attribution but add telemetry flags and a prominent console alert C) auto-create a project stub for projectless keys under org-managed sandbox project.
anya: I prefer A for safety, but we need telemetry to know impact. If we do A we must surface a clear console banner: "X% of your org usage is un-attributed - update keys or set project header".
jordyn: +1 for console banner. Also, can we add a dashboard filter for "projectless" so SREs can quickly triage? Right now rows get mixed into default project aggregates.
samir: Implementationally, changing attribution is cheap: in routing middleware replace fallback assignment with tagging request as `project: null` and set `billing_bucket: org_unattributed`. But we then need to ensure existing billing pipeline accepts null project ids.
lee: We need a migration plan if we change billing shape - analytics, billing exports, BigQuery schemas, and retention queries will break. Ops/finance must be in loop.
anya: Telemetry proposal: add `x-routing-reason` enum to traces (values: explicit_claim, header, origin, fallback_org, projectless_builtin) and emit `project_present: true|false` in tokens metric. That keeps the event model stable.
morgan: That sounds reasonable. Who owns the console banner and dashboard filter? Product or DevEx?
jordyn: Product can design copy + UX, DevEx implements dashboard filter and banner. I can take the filter tile if someone owns the backend flag.
samir: I'll own the routing middleware change behind a feature flag. I'll also add the trace attribute. Timeline: flag by EOD Friday, enable opt-in for internal canaries next week.
lee: Add a rollout playbook: (1) dark launch telemetry for two days (2) enable projectless tagging for 5% org traffic (3) surface banner to org admins (4) widen to 100% after 72h and finance signoff.
anya: Also add unit tests and a small integ test that simulates `sk_projless_*` keys and ensures no silent attribution to a third-party project's quota.
morgan: One UX ask from support: when we show the banner, include a one-click mapping flow: "Map projectless keys to an existing project" or "Create sandbox project". That reduces tickets.
jordyn: Agree. That mapping flow should annotate the key metadata so routing can pick it up without re-issuing keys. Quick API: `POST /orgs/:org/keys/:key_id/map-project {project_id}` will be enough.
samir: I'll add a small metadata field `mapped_project_id` and routing will check that first. No token rotation required.
lee: Ops-bot: mark this thread as action-items assigned: samir -> middleware flag, jordyn -> dashboard filter, anya -> telemetry schema, morgan -> support copy, lee -> rollout plan.
ops-bot: [automated] Created ticket INF-4729: "Projectless key attribution - routing, telemetry, dashboard & UX" assigned to owners, priority P2.
morgan: Thanks. Can we sync tomorrow 9am to walk the playbook? :calendar:
samir: Yup, I'll bring a patch and a diagram of the middleware flow.
anya: I'll prep the telemetry PR and proto changes.
jordyn: I'll mock the dashboard filter tile and give copy suggestions.
lee: Noted. If anyone hits edge-cases (signed headers, proxies, service-account impersonation paths) drop them in this thread.
morgan: one more: we also need to think about rate-limits that are token-level vs project-level. If we stop attributing, token rate-limits still exist - confirm behavior.
samir: Good call - rate-limit keys are applied at key-id scope before attribution. We'll keep that. We'll document difference in rollout notes.
morgan: Perfect. Closing for now, see you at sync. :thumbsup:
